problem: Prior VLN agents describe navigable candidates with whole-view features or object-centric features (detected objects or tags). These features are not discriminative enough. For example, two candidate views of the same room type ('dining room') that share common objects ('lamp', 'light') are hard to tell apart when matching them to high-level instructions, and the learned alignment generalizes poorly to unseen environments.
motivation: Humans reason with knowledge that goes beyond what they see. Language-described facts about object attributes and inter-object relations (e.g., <light hanging over kitchen island>) are complementary to visual features, help align visual objects with instruction concepts, and should improve generalization to unseen houses. This matters most for high-level, object-goal instructions such as REVERIE and SOON.
key_idea: Retrieve region-level language 'facts' (attribute-object pairs and subject-predicate-object triplets from Visual Genome) for each view with CLIP. Then inject them into DUET's candidate-view and map-history representations through instruction-guided purification, vision/history-fact cross-attention, and instruction-guided aggregation.
insight: The ablation on REVERIE val-unseen (Table 4) shows the interaction modules carry most of the gain. Without purification SR is 49.43 vs 50.44 for the full model and 46.98 for the DUET baseline. Removing either the vision-fact or the history-fact interaction costs about 1-1.5 SR (48.96 / 49.33). Fact vs object tags (Table 5) indicates what matters: VinVL object tags encoded with the same CLIP-T pipeline already recover much of the SR gain (49.73), but barely improve SPL (33.95 vs 35.38) or RGSPL (23.40 vs 24.45). This suggests that relational/attribute facts, with their larger semantic space, mainly improve path efficiency and grounding. Region granularity has a sweet spot: 5 crops beat 1 and 9 (SR 50.44 vs 49.67 / 48.99). The fallback termination policy, which returns to the node with maximum stop probability, matters a lot on SOON (SR 38.05 vs 35.23 without it) but little on REVERIE and R2R.
method: Knowledge base: parse Visual Genome region annotations into 'attribute-object' pairs and 'subject-predicate-object' triplets, canonicalize them to synsets and deduplicate, giving 630K language facts (following Kuo et al. 2022).

Fact retrieval: crop each of the 36 panorama view images into 5 sub-regions and encode each with the CLIP ViT-B/16 image encoder as a query. All facts are encoded with the CLIP text encoder as keys. The top-5 facts by cosine similarity are kept per sub-region, giving 25 fact features E_n and 5 region features R_n per view.

Purification module: compute a fact-instruction relevance matrix A=(E_n W1)(L W2)^T/sqrt(d) and take a row-wise max over instruction tokens to get one weight per fact. Each fact feature is scaled by its weight; region features R_n and history features H_n (topological-map node embeddings) are purified the same way.

Fact-aware interaction: two separate 2-layer cross-modal transformers (cross-attention then self-attention, hidden size 768, LXMERT-initialized) perform vision-fact and history-fact interaction, producing knowledge-enhanced R''_n and H''_n.

Instruction-guided aggregation: softmax attention driven by the instruction [CLS] feature pools the K=5 sub-region features into r̄_n, and likewise h̄_n. An FFN fuses them into a knowledge-enhanced view representation that is fed to DUET's dual-scale graph transformer (language/panorama/coarse/fine encoders with 9/2/4/4 layers).

Training: pretraining with MLM, masked view/region classification, single-step action prediction, and object grounding. REVERIE uses 100k iterations with DUET's synthesized augmented data; R2R uses 200k iterations with PREVALENT augmented data; SOON uses 40k iterations on original data. Fine-tuning uses DAgger-style imitation learning with a pseudo-interactive shortest-path demonstrator, plus the OG loss where objects are annotated.

Inference: at each step pick a node on the global topological map or stop. Hitting max steps (15 for REVERIE/R2R, 20 for SOON) forces a stop and returns to the node with maximum stop probability, where the highest-scoring object is selected.

setting.backbone: DUET dual-scale graph transformer (LXMERT-initialized, fine-tuned) + KERM fact modules (2-layer cross-modal transformers, LXMERT-init); frozen CLIP ViT-B/16 for fact retrieval and region/fact encoding; ViT-B/16 (ImageNet) view/object features; BUTD detector for SOON
setting.training_data: REVERIE + DUET-synthesized augmented REVERIE data (pretrain); R2R + PREVALENT augmented R2R data (pretrain); SOON original data with auto-cleaned boxes; external knowledge base of 630K facts parsed from Visual Genome; LXMERT and CLIP pretrained weights
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discrete views), with CLIP features of 5 sub-regions per view, retrieved text facts, and object features (annotated boxes on REVERIE, BUTD-detected on SOON)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (select any navigable node on the built topological map, or stop) + object selection for grounding
setting.privileged: none beyond the standard discrete nav-graph setting (REVERIE uses the dataset's provided candidate object bounding boxes, as is standard)

numbers_note: SOON is reported only on val unseen; the appendix mentions a SOON test split but gives no scores for it. The text claims a +5.52% SR gain over DUET on REVERIE val seen, but the table gives 76.88 vs 71.75 (+5.13). On REVERIE test unseen, KERM's SR 52.43 is bolded but is slightly below DUET's 52.51 in the same table. R2R comparisons use a reproduced DUET† (71.52 SR val unseen), not DUET's published 72. The ablation baseline row equals DUET's published REVERIE val-unseen numbers.
results: On REVERIE val unseen, KERM reaches SR 50.44, SPL 35.38 and RGSPL 24.45, vs DUET's 46.98 / 33.73 / 23.03. On REVERIE test unseen it reaches SPL 39.21 and RGSPL 23.64, vs DUET's 36.06 / 22.06, though SR is flat (52.43 vs 52.51). On SOON val unseen it improves SR from 36.28 to 38.05 and RGSPL from 3.75 to 4.04 over DUET. On R2R the gains over the reproduced DUET are small: SR 71.95 vs 71.52 on val unseen, and 69.73 SR / 59.25 SPL vs 69.25 / 58.68 on test unseen.
limitations: Gains on R2R are marginal (~0.4-0.5 SR over the reproduced DUET), and REVERIE test-unseen SR does not improve over DUET. Most of the benefit shows up on high-level, object-goal instructions.

It only addresses discrete nav-graph VLN; the authors list continuous environments as future work. It adds a per-view CLIP retrieval over a 630K-fact Visual Genome knowledge base (25 facts per view), which may be noisy or out of domain for indoor scenes.
The model checkpoint is selected by SPL on val unseen, and the method relies on DUET's augmented data and termination policy; the termination policy alone accounts for about 2.8 SR on SOON.
